subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What durable identity should OpenClaw use as the inbound-media isolation boundary across save, resolve, stage, cleanup, and plugin APIs?
rationale: The source evidence proves the flat media pool remains, but choosing account, resolved agent, session, channel/chat, tenant, or indexed provenance is a security and compatibility decision automation should not invent.

options.title: Adopt scoped managed media contract
options.body: Define a core scoped-media contract and update bundled channels, resolvers, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests together.

options.title: Start with account/channel subdirs
options.body: Use sanitized channel/account identifiers as the first isolation step while accepting that session/chat/tenant provenance remains follow-up work.

options.title: Defer to media provenance design
options.body: Keep this tracker open until maintainers choose a media-index or provenance schema rather than changing the filesystem layout first.

recommendation.title: Adopt scoped managed media contract
recommendation.body: Define a core scoped-media contract and update bundled channels, resolvers, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests together.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is on the central media-reference, media-store, and sandbox-staging surfaces.
